newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: FOCUS-CSR looks for full year profit boost.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-CSR looks for full year profit boost.

text.p: Diversified industrial and mining company CSR Ltd said on Monday it was budgeting for a significant increase in full year profit in 1997/98, but warned shareholders of difficulties faced by the business.
Chairman Alan Coates said after the annual general meeting the first quarter to June 30 had been "very much stronger" than the first quarter last year.
"In percentage terms, it's a very significant increase in profit we are budgeting for (in the full year)," he told reporters.
Coates earlier told the meeting that CSR remained a price taker in the sugar, timber and aluminium markets.
Current year profits from aluminium and alumina would be below those for 1996/97 (April-March), while the timber division would not be a big profit earner for the next two years.
Profits from sugar were holding up reasonably well, as the world sugar price had not fallen as much as expected and the Australian dollar had declined, Coates said.
"The growth is going to come from building materials and construction materials, not from commodities," he said.
Analysts are expecting CSR to record a full-year pre-abnormals profit to March 31, 1998 above A$290 million, after a sharp fall in net profit in 1997 to A$212 million.
However, Coates said shareholders should not expect a great deal of growth in these sectors in Australia, a mature market with low population growth.
"There's no way we will get extraordinary profits out of those groups," he said.
"They will improve as markets improve but they will go down as sure as night follows day when we get into another slump."

Coates said full year profits from CSR's American operations would be about the same as last year despite organic growth because of the A$345 million sale of its American Aggregates quarrying business in May.

"Allowing for that, America will have another good year, at about the same level as last year ex-American Aggregates," he said, adding that interest costs would be lower overall because of the repayment of debt from the Aggregates proceeds.
CSR America continued to be open to expansion, but would concentrate for now on the building of a new cement plant in Florida for about A$100 million.
The U.S. unit would also look in the long run at expanding into South America.
Coates, who was to retire after the meeting to be replaced by Ian Burgess, also strongly denied suggestions of a rift between the board and managing director Geoff Kells.
Recent reports that Burgess and Kells were at loggerheads were "utter, utter rot", he said.
Kells declined to speak to reporters after the meeting.
Elsewhere, Coates said CSR would struggle to frank its dividends by more than 50 percent over the next three to four years as a large portion of earnings would come from offshore.

He also said CSR and Mackay Refined Sugars Pty Ltd, a joint venture between the Mackay Sugar Cooperative and international commodities firm E.D.& F. Man, had reached an agreement on industry rationalisation.

The agreement, which would go a long way to resolving problems in the industry, was before the Australian Competition and Consumer Coates earlier criticised the regulator, telling shareholders it was applying rules "a bit too severely and a bit too according-to-the-book".
Earlier attempts by CSR and other sugar refiners to jointly cut supply and cooperate have been rejected by the ACCC.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
